verses.zh: 到了第八天，摩西召了亚伦和他儿子，并以色列的众长老来，
verses.en: On the eighth day[NOTE:1] Moses summoned[NOTE:2] Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel,
notes: This eighth day is the one after the seven days of ordination referred to in Lev 8:33-35.
Heb “called to”; CEV, NLT “called together.”
verses.commentary:
9:1 "on the eighth day" This would be the culmination of the "seven days" of ordination mentioned in
Leviticus 8 (i.e., Lev. 8:33,35).

▣ "Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel" Many assume that this is the group that
is referred to in Lev. 8:1-3, but this is not certain (cf. Num. 7:2). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: AARON AND HIS SONS
and SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDER.

verses.zh: 对亚伦说：「你当取牛群中的一只公牛犊作赎罪祭，一只公绵羊作燔祭，都要没有残疾的，献在耶和华面前。
verses.en: and said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both flawless, and present them before the Lord.
verses.commentary:
9:2 "Take for yourself a calf, a bull, for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without defect, and offer them
before the Lord" This is the only place in all of the sacrificial regulations that a
calf (BDB 722) is mentioned. The rabbis assume that this refers to a special sacrifice that Aaron needed to
perform because of his sin of the golden calf in Exodus 32 (another use of BDB 722).

▣ "without defect" There are several Hebrew words which are used to describe an animal "blameless" or
"without defect." The symbolism is that the animal was not physically marred, and, therefore, it stood as
a representative of a sinless, innocent life. This symbolism is fulfilled as the sinless Jesus Christ bore our
sins on Calvary (cf. 2 Cor. 5:21). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WITHOUT BLEMISH and
SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH.

▣ "before the Lord" This phrase means "at the Tabernacle."
For "Lord" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

verses.zh: 你也要对以色列人说：『你们当取一只公山羊作赎罪祭，又取一只牛犊和一只绵羊羔，都要一岁、没有残疾的，作燔祭，
verses.en: Then tell the Israelites: ‘Take a male goat[NOTE:1] for a sin offering and a calf and a lamb, both a year old and flawless,[NOTE:2] for a burnt offering,
notes: Heb “a he-goat of goats.”
Heb “and a calf and a lamb, sons of a year, flawless”; KJV, ASV, NRSV “without blemish”; NASB, NIV “without defect”; NLT “with no physical defects.”
verses.commentary:
9:3 "Then to the sons of Israel you shall speak, saying" There is both a sacrifice for Aaron and his sons
(Lev. 9:8) and a sacrifice for the people (Lev. 9:15-18).

verses.zh: 又取一只公牛，一只公绵羊作平安祭，献在耶和华面前，并取调油的素祭，因为今天耶和华要向你们显现。』
verses.en: and an ox and a ram for peace offerings to sacrifice before the Lord, and a grain offering mixed with olive oil, for today the Lord is going to appear[NOTE:1] to you.’”
notes: The verb is either a prophetic perfect (“will appear to you”) as in the MT (cf. IBHS §30.5.1.e; so many English versions), or a futurum instans participle (“is going to appear to you”) as in the LXX and several other versions (see the BHS footnote; cf. IBHS 627 §37.6f). In either case, the point is that Moses was anticipating that the Lord would indeed appear to them on this day (cf. vv. 6, 22-24).
verses.commentary:
9:4 "an ox and a ram for peace offerings. . .for today the Lord shall appear to you"
The peace offering was a symbolic way of depicting having fellowship with YHWH. On this occasion YHWH would
physically manifest Himself, probably through the Shekinah cloud, as He had done at the final erection of
the Tabernacle in Exod. 40:34-38; Num. 9:15-23. The people and the priests each had to be prepared before
He would appear to them. This was a sign of YHWH's acceptance.

verses.zh: 于是他们把摩西所吩咐的，带到会幕前；全会众都近前来，站在耶和华面前。
verses.en: So they took what Moses had commanded to the front of[NOTE:1] the Meeting Tent, and the whole congregation presented them and stood before the Lord.
notes: Heb “to the faces of.”
verses.commentary:
9:5 "stood before the Lord" In light of Lev. 9:24, what does this VERB (BDB 763, KB 840,
Qal IMPERFECT with waw) imply? The Qal stem (#1, d) is used to present oneself before

- human leaders

- Joseph ‒ Gen. 43:15

- Pharaoh ‒ Exod. 9:10

- Moses ‒ Num. 27:2

- Eleazar ‒ Num. 27:21

- YHWH

- Gen. 18:22; 19:27

- Lev. 9:5

- Deut. 4:10; 10:8,10; 19:17

It, therefore (depending on the context), can reflect

- respect

- worship

- service

verses.zh: 摩西说：「这是耶和华吩咐你们所当行的；耶和华的荣光就要向你们显现。」
verses.en: Then Moses said, “This is what the Lord has commanded you to do[NOTE:1] so that the glory of the Lord may appear[NOTE:2] to you.”
notes: Heb “which the Lord commanded you shall/should do.”

Heb “and the glory of the Lord will appear,” but the construction with the simple vav (ו) plus the imperfect/jussive (וְיֵרָא, veyeraʾ; literally, “and he will appear”) suggests purpose in this context, not just succession of events (i.e., “so that he might appear”).
verses.commentary:
9:6 "that the glory of the Lord may appear to you" The Shekinah cloud symbolized
the presence God had over the Tabernacle in Exod. 30:34-38 (cf. Exod. 29:43,45; Lev. 9:22-23; Num. 9:15-23),
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT).

verses.zh: 摩西对亚伦说：「你就近坛前，献你的赎罪祭和燔祭，为自己与百姓赎罪，又献上百姓的供物，为他们赎罪，都照耶和华所吩咐的。」
verses.en: Moses then said to Aaron, “Approach the altar and make your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement on behalf of yourself and on behalf of the people;[NOTE:1] and also make the people’s offering and make atonement on behalf of them just as the Lord has commanded.”
notes: Instead of “on behalf of the people,” the LXX has “on behalf of your house” as in the Hebrew text of Lev 16:6, 11, 17. Many commentaries follow the LXX here (e.g., J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:578; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 118) as do a few English versions (e.g., NAB), but others argue that, as on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16), the offerings of the priests also effected the people, even though there was still the need to have special offerings made on behalf of the people as reflected in the second half of the verse (e.g., B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 56).
verses.commentary:
9:7 "Moses then said to Aaron" This verse has five IMPERATIVES.

- come near ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, Qal (special usage for the priests who approach YHWH by service in the Tabernacle)

- offer ‒ lit. "do"/"make" ‒ BDB793, KB 889, Qal (only priests could do this)

- Same as 2.

- make atonement ‒ lit. "cover" ‒ BDB 497, KB 493, Piel, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ATONEMENT

- Same as 4.

Notice these are not Moses' words, but YHWH's (i.e., the last phrase).

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA, NET, Peshitta
"for the people"

NJB
"your family"

REB
"your household"

LXX
"your house"

The UBS Text Project, p. 172, gives "and for the people" a "B" rating (some doubt). There are several
places where "for his household" does appear in Leviticus (cf. Lev. 16:6,11,17,24).

When all of Lev. 9:7 is read, the NASB option is best.

verses.zh: 于是，亚伦就近坛前，宰了为自己作赎罪祭的牛犊。
verses.en: So Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the sin-offering calf which was for himself.
verses.commentary:
9:8 "sin offering. . .burnt offering. . .peace offering" We learn from Leviticus 1-7 that these particular
types of sacrifices were often offered in a series. Here, we have the series of the sin offering, the burnt
offering, and the peace offering. This seems to symbolize the order:

- the sin offering to restore relationship with God

- the burnt offering to commit oneself to God

- the peace offering, where God symbolically ate and fellowshipped with the offerer

This first series was for the priesthood.

verses.zh: 亚伦的儿子把血奉给他，他就把指头蘸在血中，抹在坛的四角上，又把血倒在坛脚那里。
verses.en: Then Aaron’s sons presented the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, and the rest of the blood he poured out at the base of the altar.
verses.commentary:
9:9 "and poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar" From Lev. 4:5-7, we understand that this
blood should have been taken into the Holy Place and sprinkled before the veil but, as of this point, the
priests, including Aaron, had not entered the inner sanctuary of the Tabernacle and, therefore, all of these
procedures were performed at the altar of sacrifice at the door of the Tabernacle.

verses.zh: 惟有赎罪祭的脂油和腰子，并肝上取的网子，都烧在坛上，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的；
verses.en: The fat and the kidneys and the protruding lobe of[NOTE:1] the liver from the sin offering he offered up in smoke on the altar just as the Lord had commanded Moses,
notes: Heb “from.”
verses.commentary:
9:10 As the blood (see SPECIAL TOPIC:
BLOOD) represented "life," the fat represented health and prosperity. Both were uniquely given to YHWH alone.

▣ "on the altar" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE.

verses.zh: 又用火将肉和皮烧在营外。
verses.en: but the flesh and the hide he completely burned up[NOTE:1] outside the camp.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he burned with fire,” an expression which is sometimes redundant in English, but here means “burned up,” “burned up entirely.”

See Lev 4:5-12 and the notes there regarding the sin offering for priest(s). The distinction here is that the blood of the sin offering for the priests was applied to the horns of the burnt offering altar in the court of the tabernacle, not the incense altar inside the tabernacle tent itself. See the notes on Lev 8:14-15.

verses.zh: 亚伦宰了燔祭牲，他儿子把血递给他，他就洒在坛的周围，
verses.en: He then slaughtered the burnt offering, and his sons[NOTE:1] handed[NOTE:2] the blood to him, and he splashed[NOTE:3] it against the altar’s sides.
notes: For smoothness in the English translation, “his” was used in place of “Aaron’s.”

The verb is a Hiphil form of מָצָא, matsaʾ, “to find” (i.e., causative, literally “to cause to find,” but here the meaning is “to hand to” or “pass to”; see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 117-18, and J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:581-82). The distinction between this verb and “presented” in v. 9 above (see the note there) is that in v. 9 Aaron’s sons held the bowl while Aaron manipulated some of the blood at the altar, while here in v. 12 they simply handed the bowl to him so he could splash all the blood around on the altar (Milgrom, 581).
For “splashed” (also in v. 18) see the note on Lev 1:5.

verses.zh: 又把燔祭一块一块地、连头递给他，他都烧在坛上；
verses.en: The burnt offering itself they handed[NOTE:1] to him by its parts, including the head,[NOTE:2] and he offered them up in smoke on the altar,
notes: See the note on v. 12.
Heb “and the burnt offering they handed to him to its parts and the head.”

verses.zh: 又洗了脏腑和腿，烧在坛上的燔祭上。
verses.en: and he washed the entrails and the legs and offered them up in smoke on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
verses.commentary:
9:14 "wash" This VERB (BDB 934, KB 1220) is used of several types of ceremonial purification.

- Aaron's sons

- priests ‒ Exod. 29:4; lev. 8:6; 16:4,24,26,28; Num. 19:7-8

- Levites ‒ Num. 8:7,21

- clothes

- priests ‒ Lev. 6:27

- Israelites

(1) touch an unclean thing ‒ Leviticus 11; 14; 17; Numbers 19

(2) involved in leprosy of some kind ‒ Leviticus 13-14

- sacrifices ‒ Lev. 1:9,13,14

Cleansing could involve

- sacrifice

- fire

- water

- temporal (?) separation

verses.zh: 他奉上百姓的供物，把那给百姓作赎罪祭的公山羊宰了，为罪献上，和先献的一样；
verses.en: Then he presented the people’s offering. He took the sin-offering male goat which was for the people, slaughtered it, and performed a purification rite with it[NOTE:1] like the first one.[NOTE:2]
notes: The expression “and performed a purification rite [with] it” reads literally in the MT, “and purified [with] it.” The verb is the Piel of חָטָא (khataʾ, Qal = “to sin”), which means “to decontaminate, purify” (i.e., “to de-sin”; see the note on Lev 8:15).

The phrase “like the first one” at the end of the verse refers back to the sin offering for the priests described in vv. 8-11 above. The blood of the sin offering of the common people was applied to the burnt offering altar just like that of the priests.

verses.zh: 也奉上燔祭，照例而献。
verses.en: He then presented the burnt offering, and did it according to the standard regulation.[NOTE:1]
notes: The term “standard regulation” (מִשְׁפָּט, mishpat) here refers to the set of regulations for burnt offering goats in Lev 1:10-13. Cf. KJV “according to the manner”; ASV, NASB “according to the ordinance”; NIV, NLT “in the prescribed way”; CEV “in the proper way.”

verses.zh: 他又奉上素祭，从其中取一满把，烧在坛上；这是在早晨的燔祭以外。
verses.en: Next he presented the grain offering, filled his hand with some of it, and offered it up in smoke on the altar in addition to the morning burnt offering.[NOTE:1]
notes: The latter part of the verse (“in addition to the morning burnt offering”) refers to the complex of morning (and evening) burnt and grain offerings that was the daily regulation for the tabernacle from the time of its erection (Exod 40:29). The regulations for it were appended to the end of the section of priestly consecration regulations in Exod 29 (see Exod 29:38-40) precisely because they were to be maintained throughout the priestly consecration period and beyond (Lev 8:33-36). Thus, the morning burnt and grain offerings would already have been placed on the altar before the inaugural burnt and grain offerings referred to here.
verses.commentary:
9:17 "filled his hand with some of it and offered it up in smoke on the altar" Only a small portion of
the grain offering was offered on the altar and the rest became food for the priests. The rabbis say that it was
three fingers tall, or one handful. Here is another example of a small part representing the whole. This is true of

- the Sabbath representing all of life

- the tithe representing all of our resources

- the firstfruits representing all of our produce

- the firstborn representing all of our children

▣ "besides the burnt offering of the morning" This could refer to

- the regular morning and evening sacrifices, called "the continual" (cf. Exod. 29:38-42; see NET, p. 231, #21)

- more probably from this context, the offerings for Aaron and his sons, mentioned in Lev. 9:8-14

verses.zh: 亚伦宰了那给百姓作平安祭的公牛和公绵羊。他儿子把血递给他，他就洒在坛的周围；
verses.en: Then he slaughtered the ox and the ram—the peace-offering sacrifices which were for the people—and Aaron’s sons handed[NOTE:1] the blood to him, and he splashed it against the altar’s sides.
notes: See the note on Lev 9:12.

verses.zh: 又把公牛和公绵羊的脂油、肥尾巴，并盖脏的脂油与腰子，和肝上的网子，都递给他；
verses.en: As for the fat parts from the ox and from the ram[NOTE:1] (the fatty tail, the fat covering the entrails,[NOTE:2] the kidneys, and the protruding lobe of the liver),
notes: Heb “And the fat from the ox and from the ram.”
The text here has only the participle “the cover” or “that which covers,” which is elliptical for “the fat which covers the entrails” (see Lev 3:3, 9, 14; 7:3).

verses.zh: 把脂油放在胸上，他就把脂油烧在坛上。
verses.en: they[NOTE:1] set those on the breasts, and he offered the fat parts up in smoke on the altar.
notes: The plural “they” refers to the sons of Aaron (cf. v. 18). The LXX, Smr, and Syriac have singular “he,” referring to Aaron alone as in the latter half of the verse (the singular is followed here by NLT). Cf. NCV “Aaron’s sons put them.”
verses.commentary: 9:20 "they" This seems to refer to the sons of Aaron, and not Aaron himself. NJB, following the LXX, has "he."

verses.zh: 胸和右腿，亚伦当作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，都是照摩西所吩咐的。
verses.en: Finally Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the Lord just as Moses had commanded.
verses.commentary:
9:21 The priests received back some meat from the sin offerings for their food (cf. Lev. 7:30-34). The LXX
and Targum of Jonathan specify that the initial command was from YHWH (Lev. 9:7).

▣ "wave offering" See note at Lev. 8:27,29.

verses.zh: 亚伦向百姓举手，为他们祝福。他献了赎罪祭、燔祭、平安祭就下来了。
verses.en: Then Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them and descended from making the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering.
verses.commentary:
9:22 The act of lifting the hands can have several connotations.

- oath taking ‒ Gen. 14:22; Exod. 6:8; Num. 14:30; Ps. 106:26; Ezek. 20:5-6

- blessing ‒ Lev. 9:22; Ps. 28:2; 63:4; 134:2; 1 Tim. 2:8

- rebellion ‒ 2 Sam. 20:21 ("hand" as ANE symbol of power; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND)

- prayer ‒ Lam. 2:19; for YHWH to act ‒ Ps. 10:12; 17:7

- praise ‒ Ps. 119:148

▣ "Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them" The lifting of the hands and eyes toward
heaven is the posture of Jewish prayer in the Old Testament and the New Testament. The exact content of Aaron's blessing
is uncertain. Many of us assume that the Aaronic blessing, found in Num. 6:22-27, may have been the core of the kind of
blessing given here (note, "May His face shine upon you," i.e., the appearance of the Shekinah cloud).

verses.zh: 摩西、亚伦进入会幕，又出来为百姓祝福，耶和华的荣光就向众民显现。
verses.en: Moses and Aaron then entered into the Meeting Tent. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people.
verses.commentary:
9:23 "Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting" This is the first time that they had entered the
inner shrine. Notice that at this point, the glory of the Lord appeared to all of the people (cf. Exod. 14:19; 19:18).

verses.zh: 有火从耶和华面前出来，在坛上烧尽燔祭和脂油；众民一见，就都欢呼，俯伏在地。
verses.en: Then fire went out from the presence of the Lord[NOTE:1] and consumed the burnt offering and the fat parts on the altar, and all the people saw it, so they shouted loudly and fell down with their faces to the ground.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from to the faces of the Lord.” The rendering here is based on the use of “my faces” and “your faces” referring to the very “presence” of the Lord in Exod 33:14-15.

Heb “fell on their faces.” Many English versions and commentaries render here “shouted for joy” (e.g., NIV; cf. NCV, NLT) or “shouted joyfully,” but the fact the people “fell on their faces” immediately afterward suggests that they were frightened as, for example, in Exod 19:16b; 20:18-21.
verses.commentary:
9:24 "Then the fire came out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering"
It is obvious that the Shekinah cloud, which first appears in Exodus, was a pillar of fire by night and a pillar of cloud by
day. The fire (the symbol of the presence of YHWH) came out from the cloud (or holy of holies) and totally consumed the
offerings on the altar. It was God's way of saying that He affirmed what they had done. We find this action several times in
the Old Testament (cf. Num. 11:3; 16:35; Jdgs. 6:21; 1 Kgs. 18:38; 2 Chr. 7:1). This will be a foreshadowing of the tragedy
that will occur in Leviticus 10.

▣ "and fell on their faces" This was a physical symbol of worship and subservience in the presence of
Deity (i.e., a theophany, like Exodus 19).

The AB, p. 591, makes the point that "fell on their faces" may denote a kneeling, while "prostrate
oneself" may refer to being flat on the ground (cf. Jos. 5:14; 1 Sam. 20:41; 2 Sam. 9:2; 14:22; Job 1:20; Ruth 2:10,
where the two terms occur in a sequence.

▣ "they shouted" This VERB (BDB 943, KB 1247) is used of

- joy ‒ Job 38:7; Ps. 35:27; Isa. 12:6; 24:14; 35:6; 42:11; 44:23; 49:13; 54:1; Jer. 31:7; Zeph. 3:14

- distress ‒ Isa. 65:14; Lam. 2:19

- here, of awe

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is "the glory of the Lord"?

- Why was its appearance so theologically significant?

- What does the "horns of the altar" (Lev. 9:9) signify?

- Why is the Aaronic blessing of Num. 6:24-27 possibly part of the blessing here?

- How does Lev. 9:24 introduce chapter 10?

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must
not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Notice that there are two sacrificial procedures.

- for the priests, Lev. 9:8 (v. 2)

- for the people, Lev. 9:15,18 (vv. 3-4)

- Notice the different types of sacrifices.

- a bull calf, for a sin offering, Lev. 9:2

- a ram, for a burnt offering, Lev. 9:2

- a male goat, for a sin offering, Lev. 9:3

- a calf and a lamb (both one year old), for a burnt offering, Lev. 9:3

- an ox and a ram, for a peace offering, Lev. 9:4

- a grain offering, Lev. 9:4

Usually sacrifices were offered in a series. Each of them representing a different purpose. See

SACRIFICES IN MESOPOTAMIA AND ISRAEL AND THEIR SIGNIFICANCE.

- Both Leviticus 9 and 10 occur on the eighth day, the day when the Aaronic priesthood begins their service at the inner shrine.

- There is a similar ritual between

- these first sacrifices for the priests and the people

- the Day of Atonement in Leviticus 16

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 9:1-7

2and he said to Aaron, "Take for yourself a calf, a bull, for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering,
both without defect, and offer them before the Lord. 3Then to
the sons of Israel you shall speak, saying, 'Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both one year old,
without defect, for a burnt offering, 4and an ox and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before the
Lord, and a grain offering mixed with oil; for today the Lord
will appear to you.'" 5So they took what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the
whole congregation came near and stood before the Lord. 6Moses said,
"This is the thing which the Lord has commanded you to do, that the glory of the
